name: Carrington Mortgage Services
desc:
Default Invoice Coordinator I | $20.00-$21.50/hr | Data Entry/Admin, No Sales Expectations
Company: Carrington Mortgage Services
Industry: Mortgage Loan Servicing / Default Servicing
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 Think of yourself as the checkpoint that makes sure vendors actually get paid correctly for work they did on a property in default (meaning a home loan that's behind on payments). You'd review invoices from vendors, compare them against what the agency or company allows, and check the supporting documentation to confirm the work billed actually matches the work completed. When something doesn't add up, you'd reach out to resolve the discrepancy directly with the vendor. This is detail-heavy, numbers-focused work that also means staying current on servicing rules from agencies like FHA, VA, USDA, and Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac, so it rewards someone who's comfortable both crunching numbers and learning regulatory detail over time.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High School Diploma or equivalent required. Some college education preferred.
Required Experience: None required outright. Six months to one year of billing or invoicing experience preferred.
Preferred Experience: Default mortgage servicing experience and understanding of loan servicing default-related documents.
Required Skills:
Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Attention to detail and strong organizational skills
Ability to research within applicable systems to find supporting documentation
Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-production environment
Ability to work independently and organize your own workflow
Basic math skills (add, subtract, multiply, divide) with speed and accuracy processing numerical data
Comfortable communicating by phone
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone detail-oriented who genuinely enjoys catching discrepancies and getting numbers right
Someone comfortable in a fast-paced, high-production environment with real deadlines
Someone who can work independently and manage their own workflow without close supervision
Someone interested in building knowledge of mortgage servicing and federal loan regulations over time
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who struggles with detail-heavy, numbers-focused work for extended periods
Anyone who needs a slower-paced role without production goals
Anyone uncomfortable resolving billing disputes directly with vendors
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Invoice review and reconciliation
Vendor communication
Data verification
Attention to detail
High-volume document processing
Numerical accuracy
Independent workflow management
Deadline-driven production environment
Research and documentation review
Discrepancy resolution
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
 Application → Assessment → Phone screen → Final interview. Total time to hire averages 3 to 15 days.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell us about any experience you have with billing, invoicing, or reviewing documents for accuracy.
How do you stay organized when managing a high volume of invoices with a deadline attached?
Walk us through how you'd handle finding a discrepancy between an invoice and the supporting documentation.
What's your comfort level with basic math and processing numerical data quickly and accurately?
How do you approach learning new regulations or rules that affect how you do your job?

Notes: This is a genuinely solid entry point into mortgage servicing since no prior default servicing experience is required, just preferred, and the company offers real training and educational reimbursement to help someone grow into the role. This is Carrington's third role currently in your database alongside their Default Claims VA QA Analyst and Customer Advocate Specialist positions, worth cross-referencing tier and contact info across all three since they're the same employer.
